summary: special meeting "on Tuesday evening" to appoint a new Provost, Junior Bailie and a member for Stout's vacancy. Sinclair (proposed, seconded by W. S. Smith) beat David Sutherland "by six votes against two". Goodlad was made Provost.
election notice, poll on "TUESDAY, the Third day of NOVEMBER", nominations by Thursday 29 Oct. No vacancy count.
nominations Duncan, Hunter, Mitchell, Tulloch jr; they don't exceed the vacancies, so no poll.

Shetland Times, Sat 31 Oct 1885, p3 (art. 039, 043): adjourned meeting "on Tuesday evening" (27 Oct). Stove present. Bailie Mitchell's letter resigning and not standing again; a deputation was sent to talk him round (he stood and was re-elected).
statutory meeting. Present includes "L. G. Stove". The Clerk reported Duncan, Hunter, Mitchell and Tulloch "re-elected ... at the annual election on 3d instant". Stove re-elected a Harbour Trustee.
"The quarterly statutory meeting ... on Monday" at noon, so Mon 12 Jul 1886. Present: Bailie Robertson, Leisk, J. Robertson jr, G. Harrison, Stove, Tulloch jr. Duncan absent.

"RESIGNATION OF MR WM. DUNCAN": the Clerk read his letter; he intended to withdraw, and "three weeks hence he would cease" to have any connection with the council. A deputation (the Chairman and John Robertson jr) was sent to ask him to reconsider.
meeting on Friday evening (30 Jul). Present: Bailie Robertson, Leisk, J. Robertson jr, Stove. Duncan not there.

local news: G. Harrison, Stove, Halcrow, Leisk and Jamieson retire by rotation; "Mr Wm. Duncan has resigned, and one member will [be] disqualified", making seven vacancies at the coming election. Future tense, after the 15 Oct meeting, so John Harrison (i) was still a member then and the ledger's 1 Oct is too early.
the quarterly meeting "on Monday" (11 Oct) adjourned to Friday evening (15 Oct) because of the hour.

"RESIGNATION OF A COUNCILLOR": the deputation reported he "had definitely refused to continue in office"; G. Harrison made interim Convener of Lighting and Cleansing in his place. This matches his profile ("accepted by the council on October 15th").
"RETIRING COUNCILLORS": Stove said he would rather not stand again; the Chairman wanted Leisk, Stove and Harrison to stay.
nominations were "the five retiring councillors, thus still leaving two seats vacant", which the Council could fill afterwards.
"on Friday evening" Charles Robertson and John B. Anderson were "elected to fill the vacancies". "Yesterday" in the same column is Friday, so Friday 19 Nov 1886.
James Hunter, accountant of the Union Bank, appointed agent at Portsoy.
Shetland Times, Sat 8 Jan 1887, p3 (art. 047, 048): adjourned meeting "Tuesday evening" (4 Jan). Hunter's resignation accepted; "a constant and useful member for the last ten years".

Shetland Times, Sat 19 Mar 1887, p2 (art. 053, 054): fortnightly meeting "yesterday (Friday) evening"; Porteous elected "till the vacancy caused [by] Mr Hunter's resignation". Sworn in at the next meeting (ST 26 Mar 1887, p2, art. 040).
"RETIRING COUNCILLORS": Bailie Mitchell, Tulloch jr and A. B. Jamieson retire, plus one of the five elected last year.
vacancies from "the retirement [of] Mr Tulloch, and the departure from town [of] Mr Jamieson"; Mitchell and Anderson re-nominated, Goudie and Laing nominated, no poll.
statutory meeting "on Monday noon" (12 Nov), with Goudie and Laing present. Doesn't date the election.

"At a meeting of the Town Council, held last ..." Mitchell's resignation accepted with regret. The scan at that point reads "held last" at a line end; the word after is lost. The item above it says the Commissioners met "last night" (Friday 18 Oct).
five vacancies instead of the usual three, "one being caused by the lamented death of Mr Stove, and the other by the resignation of Bailie Mitchell". Harrison, Leisk and Halcrow retire by rotation.
Burgh of Lerwick notice of the persons nominated, and "municipal election on Tuesday next" (5 Nov).
"Next Week": "Municipal Election Voting Tuesday, in the Burgh Court Room".
a committee formed to re-elect Halcrow, [Harrison: OCR garbled] and Leisk and to elect Kay and Hunter. A contest (the wiki has the votes).
"The municipal fight is over"; Halcrow, Harrison, Leisk, Hunter and Kay returned. This is the 9th in the wiki: the day it was printed.

"Thursday first is the last day for nominating" (30 Oct); retiring Bailie Robertson (Chief Magistrate), Bailie C. Robertson, John Robertson jun. and Porteous. Poll day would be Tue 4 Nov, as in the ledger.
nominations "On Thursday" (29 Oct).
Leisk, Goudie, Laing and Tulloch took the oath at the Council Chamber on Thursday (5 Nov).
leader: "Mr Garriock is the only new member".
"MUNICIPAL ELECTION": the official figures for Goudie, Garriock, Leisk, Laing and Sutherland.

the Clerk said the retiring Councillors were "Messrs Hunter, Harrison, Halcrow, and Kay". Charles Robertson had died in July 1895, so the Nov 1895 general filled five seats: these four and his (1893 cohort, due out in 1896).
four retire in November: "Bailie Porteous, Messrs John Robertson, P. S. Goodlad, and R. B. Hunter". All four stood again.
retiring "by rotation": Bailie Goudie, Garriock, Halcrow and Laing. Leisk, the fourth of the 1894 cohort, is not on the list.
nominations: the four retiring councillors (Goudie, Garriock, Halcrow, ...) nominated again.
retiring at the next election: "Provost Leisk, Councillors Harrison, ..." (OCR breaks off).
the four retiring (Leisk, Harrison, Kay, Stove) were nominated "and no more", so "the Council therefore consists of the former members".
on Thursday "the four newly-elected Councillors" took the oath before Bailie Porteous.
retiring: Bailie Porteous, Goodlad, R. B. Hunter, John Robertson and S. Johnson (the May 1899 by-elected member, re-standing). Five seats: the 1896 four and Garriock's (died Feb 1899).

"the five vacancies" polled on Tuesday; result John Robertson, D. R. Morrison, P. S. Goodlad, A. A. Porteous (59), S. Johnson, then D. Sutherland. "The whole of the old members ... returned", Morrison taking Hunter's seat.
retiring: Bailie Goudie, Kay, Halcrow, Laing.
council meeting. The Clerk said only three Commissioners retired in rotation, so one of the others had to be chosen "to complete the full third"; "Mr Kay volunteered to retire".
"The four Councillors presently retiring having been nominated again ... there will be no contest" (Goudie, Kay, Halcrow, Laing; see the 13 Oct 1900 list in ltc-1895-1901.md §6).
same list: Provost Leisk, G. Harrison, A. S. Stove, S. Johnson.
the Clerk: the four retiring members are "the Provost and Councillors Harrison, Stove and Johnson".
"Death of Mr Alfred S. Stove": he died "On Sunday morning last" (13 Oct). Also the County Council tribute (art. 041).
Burgh notice of the candidates "at the Municipal Election on TUESDAY NEXT", i.e. 5 Nov. The DB had Fri 1 Nov.

"Municipal Election" and "THE RESULT": the three retiring (Harrison, Johnson, Leisk) plus John G. Irvine, put forward "with a view to filling the vacancy" of the late Mr Stove; James Robertson also stood, forcing a poll. Voting began on Tuesday morning; result Irvine, Harrison, Johnson, Leisk elected, Robertson 130.
"RETIRING COUNCILLORS": Bailie Porteous, Councillors Robertson, Morrison and Goodlad.
the four retiring councillors, with no other candidates, were on Tuesday "duly declared elected".
the Clerk "intimated the re-election of the four retiring Councillors".
retiring: "Bailie Goudie, and Councillors Halcrow, Kay, and Laing".
the election "took place on Tuesday last" (3 Nov). Page 1 (art. 008, 010): thanks from Ganson ("next the highest successful"), Kay, Laing and the defeated James Robertson.

the election on Tuesday filled the vacancies "caused by the retiral of Provost Leisk and Councillors Gilbert Harrison, J. G. Irvine and Sinclair Johnson"; Leisk withdrew after nomination; six candidates.
his death "in the early hours of Thursday" (2 Feb) at Victoria Wharf.
Provost Goudie's tribute at the council.
retiring: "Bailie A. A. Porteous, Councillors P. S. Goodlad, D. R. Morrison, and L. Laurenson" (Laurenson in Robertson's seat).

retiring: Bailie Laing, Ganson, Kay and J. T. J. Sinclair. "It was Provost Goudie who should have retired, but on his election to Provost, he had to serve a period of three years", so Sinclair retired, having had "the smallest number of votes" in 1904.
retiring in November: "Provost Goudie, Councillors Irvine, Harrison, and Sinclair Johnson".
Provost Goudie's "decision to retire into private life".
Provost Porteous presiding; the Clerk intimated the retiring Councillors as Goodlad, Ganson, Sinclair and Ratter (OCR garbled on the first two names; confirmed by the notice below).
election notice: four councillors "in the place of Messrs William Sinclair, Alexander Ratter, Peter S. Goodlad, and Robert D. Ganson, who retire by rotation".
Goodlad thanks the electors for returning him.
"Declaration of the Poll": Provost Porteous read the result, "the return of the former candidates" received with applause.
retiring "Bailies Laing and Stout, and Councillors J. Laing and J. Smith". The Provost (still Porteous) spoke after the list.
election notice for four councillors in place of Bailies Arthur Laurenson Laing and Robert Stout and Councillors James Laing and John Smith.
thanks notice signed Arthur L. Laing, John Smith and R. Stout for "again electing us" (the snippet; the rest of the signatures not read).
the vote on Tuesday returned "the four retiring Councillors", and the new candidate (Loggie) was left out.
"RESIGNATION OF MR J. G. IRVINE": his letter read; the Provost said he had sat since 1901. The report is of the meeting "on Tuesday night" (art. 073), i.e. 7 Dec 1909.
a special meeting "held on Tuesday night, before the ordinary meeting" (4 Jan) unanimously appointed James A. Loggie in place of Irvine, resigned.
retiring members "Provost Porteous, and Messrs A. Smith, W. S. Smith, and J. A. Loggie".
election notice, in place of Arthur A. Porteous, Provost, and three others.

"Lerwick Town Council. Election": count on the Tuesday night, "The first four were therefore declared elected". The result table itself isn't in the OCR, but the analysis says "only ten votes separating the second and fifth", which matches the DB (A. Smith 268, Groat 258). The same article reports the Friday meeting electing Bailie Laing Provost in place of ex-Provost Porteous, with Loggie and W.
"Retiring Councillors": Bailie Goodlad and Councillors Ganson, Sinclair and Ratter.
election notice for four councillors in place of Ratter, W. Sinclair, R. D. Ganson and Bailie P. S. Goodlad, "who retire by rotation".
nominations on Tuesday first for the seats of Bailie Goodlad and Councillors Ganson, Ratter and Sinclair, who were retiring.
"only the four retiring candidates had been nominated".
meeting on Thursday to swear in "the newly-elected Councillors"; present include Goodlad, Ratter, W. Sinclair, Ganson.
by Friday morning he "had reconsidered his decision to resign".
the Provost read a letter from Councillor Macdougall resigning as Town Councillor.
retiring in November: Bailie Stout, Councillors John Smith, James Laing, J. A. Loggie. Provost (Arthur) Laing is not on the list, although his 1909 cohort was due out.
monthly meeting (Tue 1 Oct 1912). Present include Provost Laing, Bailies Stout and Goodlad, Councillors Ganson, Loggie, Macdougall, Sinclair.

"Resignation of a Councillor". The automatic retirals were Stout, John Smith, James Laing and Loggie. Loggie told the paper on Tuesday he wouldn't seek re-election. "On Tuesday" (8 Oct 1912) MacDougall resigned, and the article says Loggie was then withdrawn from retiring. The later 2 Nov preview and the Nov 1912 attendance show Loggie did go out after all, so that arrangement didn't hold.
one side withdrew a candidate, so the election went uncontested.
election preview. Vacancies are caused by the retiral of Stout, John Smith, James Laing and Loggie, and "the resignation of Councillor W. Macdougall".
first meeting after the election, "Provost Laing presiding"; Stout re-appointed Bailie.

adjourned meeting (Mon 11 Nov 1912). Present: Provost Laing, Bailies Stout and Goodlad, Councillors R. D. Ganson, W. S. Smith, A. Smith, R. H. Ramsay, J. Smith, W. Sinclair, A. Ratter, J. Laing. That's 11, and Grierson (a Nov 1912 winner) makes 12.
"Retiring Councillors": Provost Laing, Bailie Goodlad, Councillors Andrew Smith and W. Spence Smith.
four members retired, six candidates for the four vacancies.
same list; "Provost Laing did not offer himself for re-election".
"The Municipal Election": Goodlad, L. Laurenson, Andrew Smith and W. S. Smith returned; the Socialist candidates defeated.
election on Tue 3 Nov. Four retiring councillors, starting with Bailie Ganson.
the four retiring members, Bailie Ganson, Councillors Alex. Ratter, Wm. Sinclair and John Smith, were renominated with no new candidates, so they were declared elected.
"Death of Provost Stout". As announced in the special edition of Saturday last, he "died with startling suddenness".
Deaths: at Helendale, Lerwick, on the 3rd.

monthly meeting (Tue 6 Jul 1915). Present: Provost Goodlad, Bailies Ganson and Ratter, Councillors J. T. J. Sinclair, J. Laing, J. Smith, W. Sinclair. The Provost refers to "the death of Councillor Grierson".

Shetland Times, Sat 7 Aug 1915, p4 (art. 093 and "Filling a Vacancy", art. 096): monthly meeting "on Tuesday evening". Proposed by J. Smith and seconded by Bailie Ganson for Grierson's vacancy; "no other proposal", so declared elected.
Deaths: at Windhouse, Lerwick, at noon on Friday 14th, Captain Laurence Laurenson.

Shetland Times, Sat 5 Aug 1916, p5 (art. 107, "Appointment of New Member"): monthly meeting "on Tuesday evening". Bailie Ganson moved Henderson for Laurenson's seat; W. Sinclair moved Magnus Manson; Henderson won "by a majority". The Provost and Ganson promised Manson "the next vacancy".

Local News, "Resignation of a Town Councillor": Andrew Smith of Islesburgh House resigned; through failing health he had not attended recently. "On Tuesday evening" Magnus L. Manson was co-opted in his room.
Same issue, p5 (art. 093 area): monthly meeting (Tue 5 Sep 1916), present includes Ramsay.

Shetland Times, Sat 11 Nov 1916, p5 (art. 098, "Resignation of a Councillor"): at the monthly meeting (Tuesday evening, 7 Nov) a letter was read from W. Spence Smith, Northness, resigning because of his health after nine years; accepted with regret.

Shetland Times, Sat 9 Dec 1916, p4 (art. 110, "The Shops' Hours", sub-head "New Councillor"): monthly meeting "on Tuesday evening"; unanimously agreed to appoint Mr H. J. Robertson (OCR garbled) in place of W. Spence Smith, "who had resigned owing to failing health".
meeting of Tue 2 Jan 1917; present include "H. J. Robertson".

"Municipal Election, 1919": poll if needed on Tuesday 4 November, to elect seven Councillors in place of James Laing and Robert Henderson Ramsay (by rotation) and J. T. J. Sinclair, J. P. Henderson, C. B. Stout, M. L. Manson and H. J. Robertson ("elected ad interim").
leader: of the seven returned, Pottinger, Morrison and Ollason were new members.
"The Result of the Poll": Laing 656, M. L. Manson 610, J. J. Pottinger 546, then Morrison, Ollason, J. T. J. Sinclair and Ramsay (matches the DB).
election notice for four councillors "in the place of" Peter S. Goodlad, Robert D. Ganson, Alexander Ratter and William Sinclair, "who retire by rotation".
Pottinger present at a Town Council meeting (the last found).

Shetland Times, Sat 7 May 1921, p4, "Lerwick Town Council": monthly meeting on Tuesday (3 May). Pottinger not among those present. (The same issue's "Goodlad elected by nine votes to six" is the Education Authority, not the Town Council.)
"Ex-Provost Goodlad" in the chair of a meeting attended by Provost Ganson.
Zetland County Council: J. T. J. Sinclair appointed to Pottinger's vacant seat for Lerwick Central (8 votes to 3 for Duffin). Pottinger had left the County Council too.

Shetland Times, Sat 11 Jun 1921, p5 (arts. 100–101), "Lerwick Town Council": monthly meeting "on Tuesday evening" (7 Jun). Under "New Councillor Elected", Manson moved William Bruce for "the vacancy caused by the retiral of Mr J. J. Pottinger"; Ramsay moved J. M. Goodlad, who "stood next to Mr Pottinger". Five votes each; the Provost's casting vote went to Goodlad. Manson noted that whoever was co
Shetland Times, Sat 9 Jul 1921, p5 (arts. 125, 128): Goodlad present on Tue 5 Jul and given "his predecessor, Mr J. J. Pottinger"'s committee places.
he would not reconsider; he could not give the time to all his other offices (Parish Council chairman, County Council, Insurance and Pensions Committees).
"Resignation of Bailie Sinclair": a letter resigning as Magistrate and Councillor read at the monthly meeting on Tuesday (4 Oct); the Provost called it "rather an unexpected resignation".

"The Greetin' Meetin'": the Clerk announced the retiring councillors as J. Smith, R. H. Ramsay, J. T. J. Sinclair and R. Ollason "in the ordinary course", J. M. Goodlad as an ad interim member, and Bailie Sinclair "in virtue of his resignation".
election notice for six councillors, same names.
local news: the retiring councillors are James Laing, M. L. Manson, James Morrison and G. H. Duffin (OCR garbled on the last name; confirmed by the notice below).
election notice: four councillors in place of Laing, Magnus Laurence Manson, Morrison and George Herbert Duffin, "who retire by rotation".
"No Poll": the four retiring councillors were renominated and returned unopposed.
the four who retire by rotation are "Provost Ganson, Bailie Ratter, and Councillors A. S. Manson and D. Murray".
election notice, same four.
the four retiring members were re-nominated, with no other nominations. (The 27 Nov 1923 poll in the adverts is the Temperance Act poll, not the council election.)
nominations "to-day (Friday)". No new candidates had been mentioned, and several men who were approached declined.
Bruce, Ollason, J. T. J. Sinclair and E. S. Reid Tait were nominated. With no new candidates, the four were "declared elected".
a letter to the editor complains that "we are to have no contest this year".
"Retiring members re-nominated. No poll."
"Retiring town councillors re-nominated". No poll for the four vacancies.
"No poll this year. Four retiring members re-nominated."
those retiring were Bailie John Campbell and Councillors M. L. Manson, G. H. Duffin and [Cogle; the snippet is cut off].
"No contest. Retiring councillors nominated."
Councillor Thomas Johnston's letter asking for six months' leave of absence; he had been laid aside by illness.
"Lerwick Town Councillor Killed". His car went off the road near Pettawater on Sunday afternoon (30 Sep 1934); the doctor found he had probably died instantly.
the monthly meeting "on Tuesday evening" (9 Oct 1934), Provost Ollason presiding.
letter from Johnston resigning "owing to ill-health"; accepted with regret.
retiring councillors are Bailies Cogle and Duffin and Councillors M. L. Manson and Thomas Johnston; "The late Councillor Laurence Sandison was also due to retire". Five vacancies.
preview. Vacancies from three retiring by rotation, "the resignation of Mr Thomas Johnston" and the death of Sandison.
"Ex-Bailie Cogle Resigns from Council". At the monthly meeting on Tuesday (5 May 1936), after the water debate, he resigned, "definitely refused to reconsider", and left the meeting.
obituary; he "passed away on Sunday morning" (28 Jun 1936).
monthly meeting "on Tuesday evening" (7 Jul 1936). T. A. Sinclair co-opted "in room of Mr L. A. Cogle, who resigned"; Duffin's seat deferred to August.
Sinclair chosen as the highest unsuccessful candidate at the last election; unanimous.

Shetland Times, Sat 8 Aug 1936, p4 (art. 068 and 074): "Mr Thomas Irvine, Confectioner, Co-opted" at the monthly meeting on Tuesday (4 Aug 1936), to the vacancy "caused by the death of ex-Bailie Duffin".

Shetland Times, Sat 8 Aug 1936, p4 (art. 068 and 074): "Mr Thomas Irvine, Confectioner, Co-opted" at the monthly meeting on Tuesday (4 Aug 1936), to the vacancy "caused by the death of ex-Bailie Duffin".
"Mr E. J. F. Clausen Co-opted to Council" at the meeting following the statutory meeting, on Tuesday evening (10 Nov 1936).
Bailie Halcrow: with no contest they "had to get a member" (the uncontested 3 Nov general left one of five seats empty).

"The result" of the 2 Nov 1937 poll (six seats): James Laing, J. J. Aitken, Wm. Anderson, J. L. Linklater, a fifth name the OCR garbles (the wiki has W. G. Smith), E. J. F. Clausen, then Dalziel and J. A. Williamson. Only the snippet was read, not the table itself; the order matches the wiki and Dalziel and Williamson being the next two co-opted in 1938.
Mr and Mrs Clausen to live in Thurso on his appointment as superintendent for Wick, Thurso, Orkney and Shetland.
at the monthly meeting "on Tuesday evening" (4 Jan 1938), a letter from Clausen, "as he had taken up duty in the South", resigning. Provost Smith said they were sorry to lose him.

"Member co-opted": "in place of Mr E. J. F. Clausen, resigned", Captain Halcrow moved and Bailie Laing seconded Peter Dalziel; unanimous. The report opens with the monthly meeting held "on Tuesday evening", i.e. Tue 1 Feb 1938, not Thu 3 Feb.
died "very suddenly on Friday afternoon of last week" (22 Jul 1938), aged 54.

"Municipal Election. Four of Retiring Candidates Returned." Polled "on Tuesday" (1 Nov). Nine candidates for five seats; the winners were Shearer (1260, the most votes ever at a municipal election), Ganson, William Sinclair (828), Dalziel and Irvine (760). Mouat (509) topped the losers, ahead of J. A. Williamson (490).

special meeting "last evening" (Fri 24 May) on the Police Act. Councillor W. G. Smith resigned verbally but agreed to reconsider; "Councillor William Sinclair tendered his resignation in writing", and he was also asked to reconsider.

"MR W. SINCLAIR ADHERES TO RESIGNATION". Bailie Laing said they should "declare the seat vacant", which was agreed. This is part of the report of the June monthly meeting (headed "Lerwick Town Council. Progress with Waste Paper Scheme", same page), whose day is garbled in the OCR ("on.sl' the day evening"); the first Tuesday was 4 Jun.
report of the monthly meeting held over to next week; "At this meeting Mr Andrew M. Mouat" was co-opted.

"NEW COUNCILLOR CO-OPTED", part of the report of the meeting "on Tuesday evening of last week" (2 Jul), Bailie Laing presiding. It was customary to co-opt the candidate next highest to the successful ones, and "Mr Andrew Mouat held that position".

"Death of Captain A. Halcrow. Sudden passing." He died at home "late on Christmas Eve" (he had been out as usual on Tuesday), and was then a member of Lerwick Town Council, the County Council and the Harbour Trust.
"Tribute to Late Captain Halcrow. Co-Option of Mr. John A. Williamson", at the Council's "meeting on Tuesday" (7 Jan 1941), Bailie Laing presiding.
"Member co-opted": Williamson was "the next highest on the list of candidates unsuccessful at last election".

ST Sat 7 Jun 1941, p2 (art. 066 and 070): at "the Council's meeting on Tuesday" (3 Jun) the Clerk read Provost Smith's letter resigning as Councillor and Provost "three weeks from this date", on account of his illness; accepted with regret. The letter's date isn't given (Shearer had learnt of it the night before the meeting).
at the meeting "on Tuesday evening" (1 Jul) Major Shearer was appointed Provost, W. G. Smith Junior Bailie, and "Mr. Arthur Johnston [Johnson] was co-opted to fill the vacancy".
the resignations of two members "who have not been able to attend meetings for some time past" were intimated "at the Council's meeting on Tuesday" (5 Aug 1941).

"RESIGNATION OF COUNCILLORS". Linklater's letter of 26 July resigned "three weeks from that date" (16 Aug 1941); he was away and saw no early return. Irvine could not attend from December 1939 because of sixteen-hour working days. The Provost took it that both resignations were accepted.
Ganson moved not to accept Linklater's (Private Linklater, in the Forces); Aitken said Linklater had always meant to leave. The vacancies were filled in October, so it was accepted.
"The co-opting of two new members ... was agreed to unanimously at Tuesday's meeting" (7 Oct 1941).

"Two vacancies fell to be filled on the Council, following the resignations of Messrs J. L. Linklater and Thomas Irvine": John Gear (proposed by Bailie Smith) and Charles Inkster (proposed by Williamson).
"Junior Bailie of Lerwick": Bailie William G. Smith died "on Saturday of last week" (28 Feb 1942) in hospital in Glasgow, aged 44.
"Town Council Special Meeting. New Bailie Appointed. T. A. SINCLAIR CO-OPTED TO COUNCIL", held "on Tuesday, 31st March".

"Resignation of Councillor Gear": the Clerk read his letter (he was now postmaster at Lyness, Orkney), accepted as he could no longer attend. Part of the report of "the monthly meeting ... on Tuesday evening" (2 Feb), same page. The OCR runs this column into a seamen's conference report.
"Councillor Co-opted": Robert Anderson (OCR "Robert D."; "R. A." everywhere else) appointed to Gear's vacancy, at the special meeting "On Thursday evening" (11 Feb), same page.

"TOWN COUNCIL TRIBUTE TO RETIRING COUNCILLOR", meeting "on Tuesday" (3 Oct): a letter from Inkster "tendering his resignation" as he was leaving for the south; the Provost didn't ask him to reconsider.
November meeting "on Tuesday evening" (7 Nov): "Mr Prophet Smith has been co-opted" for Inkster.
"COUNCILLOR DEPARTS": a letter "dated 2nd January" from Prophet Smith resigning, as he was leaving for an appointment in Greenock. Read at the monthly meeting "on Tuesday" (9 Jan), art. 047.
the monthly meeting "on Tuesday" (6 Feb) filled "the vacancy ... caused by the resignation of Mr Prophet Smith" with Alexander Morrison, Brown's Buildings.
"50 PER CENT RETIRE": Mouat, J. A. Williamson, Johnson, T. A. Sinclair, R. A. Anderson and Alexander Morrison. Present and staying on: Provost Shearer, Bailies Aitken and Dalziel, Councillor Ganson.
"TOWN COUNCIL ELECTION. FOR SIX SEATS ELEVEN CANDIDATES"; nominations closed Friday 26 Oct.
the first post-war election; "by Tuesday there was every indication of a keen fight. Fortunately, the day was fine", 1991 votes, result announced at 2.15 a.m.
"Resignation": a letter from Councillor Laing intimating his retiral, which "will come into force on the 29th of November"; Provost Shearer said he had been in poor health.
"Ex-Provost Laing's seat filled": Arthur Johnston, highest of the unsuccessful candidates at the recent election, chosen at the meeting "on Monday evening" (10 Dec 1945).

the council adjourned at its monthly meeting "on Tuesday" (5 Mar) in respect to the late Councillor David Gray, "whose passing occurred on Monday evening of this week" (4 Mar). Tribute in art. 017; public funeral notice p1 art. 069.

meeting of Tue 1 Oct 1946. The Town Clerk's list: "Bailie J. J. Aitken, Bailie P. Dalziel, and Councillors W. Anderson, Ar. Johnson, and T. A. Sinclair". Johnson "took the place of ex-Provost Laing", so counted in the one-third quota; Sinclair (co-opted for David Gray) retired as a co-opted member.
"ELECTION SELECTION": Lerwick electors "will find Tuesday's choice a difficult matter", twelve candidates for five seats (art. 048: "TWELVE NOMINATIONS: FIVE VACANCIES").
the Harbour Trust election "coincided with the municipal election on Tuesday". Result, "HOW THEY FARED" (p4 art. 061): Aitken 1221, Burgess 987, Brownlie 829, ... (matches the DB).
the Harbour Trust election "coincided with the municipal election on Tuesday". Result, "HOW THEY FARED" (p4 art. 061): Aitken 1221, Burgess 987, Brownlie 829, ... (matches the DB).

Zetland County Council meeting on Tuesday (20 May). After Mr Jamieson's resignation was accepted, "the petition for the election of Lt. Col. Shearer to the vacancy was signed by 207 persons", and he was appointed. This is the Whalsay and Skerries seat (election 692, dated 1947-05-01 in the DB). Probably why he left the town council the next month, though no article says so.
Burgh notice names a meeting of the Town Council on 1 July 1947.

monthly meeting on Tuesday (3 Jun). Present: Provost Aitken, Bailies L. W. Smith and R. A. Anderson, Councillors Burgess, W. Anderson, Peterson, Ollason, Morrison, A. Johnson and Brownlie. Shearer was not present.
"EX-BAILIE RETURNS TO COUNCIL TABLE", the report of "the monthly meeting of Lerwick Town Council on Tuesday evening" (1 Jul).
"Ex-Bailie Peter Dalziel returns to the Council in place of Lt.-Col. Magnus Shearer, who resigned last month." Dalziel had topped the losers in 1946.
standing down are "Bailie R. A. Anderson and Councillors R. J. H. Ganson, A. Morrison, and P. Dalziel who was recently co-opted to fill the vacancy left by Lt.-Col. M. Shearer".
Anderson and Morrison, the lowest of the six winners of 1945 (904 and 903), retire after two years to make up the retiring number.

elections "put back six months", so the next is on 3 May 1949. Retiring: Bailie L. W. Smith and J. G. Peterson (elected 1945); "Treasurer R. Ollason remained in office ... two years further because of his appointment last year as treasurer"; so the two lowest winners of 1946 retire, "Councillor W. S. Anderson and Councillor Arthur Johnson".
"Tuesday first is polling day in the Town Council election"
"Only seven County Council elections". There will be only seven polls "in the County Council election on 10th May".
same issue, the council's "monthly meeting on Tuesday" (13 Sep). No other meeting is reported that week, so the co-option is taken as the same meeting.

"Politics Laid Aside for Co-Option". Johnson was invited to fill the vacancy "caused by the resignation of Mr James H. Brownlie". His letter, read at the same meeting, said he had been "granted six months' leave of absence earlier this year" when ill, and was now being transferred south. So the resignation and the co-option were the same meeting (Tue 13 Sep 1949, ltc-election-dates-1949-1964.md),
"Four members retire this time— Provost J. J. Aitken, Bailie G. H. Burgess, Councillor J. D. Williamson, and Councillor Arthur Johnson."
"will therefore take place on Tuesday, 2nd May"

two petitions for "the vacancy existing in the Tingwall Division, due to the resignation of Mr George Ross", for G. M. Nelson and G. K. Spence, "who is already a member of the County Council representing South Yell". A similar by-election would follow in Yell South "if Mr Spence carries out his intention". Ross's resignation was accepted "at the Council meeting on Tuesday" (20 Jun).
"Mr Spence recently resigned his Yell seat to contest Tingwall".
South Yell nominations: Charles A. Guthrie and John Williamson, Bankend House, Ulsta.
election address to the electors of Yell South: the poll is "TUESDAY, 1st August", at East Yell Public School.
"BY-ELECTIONS": Spence 233, Nelson 106 (Tingwall); in Yell South "the former representative has been returned" (Williamson, who sat 1940–49). Matches the DB votes.
"Mr Spence having vacated membership of Yell South to contest Tingwall".

ST Fri 13 Apr 1951, p4 (art. 047 and 048): meeting of Tue 10 Apr 1951; Provost Anderson thanked "all four of the retiring members": Blance, Inkster, Morrison and Ollason (the only four nominated until Mouat stood).

ST Fri 13 Apr 1951, p4 (art. 047 and 048): meeting of Tue 10 Apr 1951; Provost Anderson thanked "all four of the retiring members": Blance, Inkster, Morrison and Ollason (the only four nominated until Mouat stood).
council business, "Bailie Inkster and Councillor Conochie".
"EIGHT CANDIDATES FOR FOUR SEATS"; the starred retiring members are Peterson, Johnson, W. S. Anderson and Conochie ("has just completed his first three-year period").
"Municipal Election Tuesday 6th May, 1952" (advert)
District Council contests "in ten days time".
"Polling day". The town has had its election, and "the county will have its turn on Tuesday first": 13 May. The baseline's 5 May is neither the town's day (6 May) nor the county's.

ST Fri 9 May 1952, p5 (art. 081, report art. 080): "SUCCESSFUL": Peterson 790, Johnson, Conochie 673, Tait; unsuccessful Robertson 603, More, W. S. Anderson 555, Davidson 492. Matches the DB (Johnson 718, Tait 662; the OCR loses those two figures).
"The four are Messrs R. A. Anderson, J. J. Aitken, G. H. Burgess, and J. D. Williamson."
"The Town Council election takes place on Tuesday first"
"THE RESULT": R. A. Anderson 1144, Burgess 1041, Eunson 973 (OCR "9713"), Gray; unsuccessful J. D. Williamson first. Matches the DB.
"eight candidates for the municipal election".

(\* = retiring member.) Text: "There are 3950 on the roll, but of these 32 are not eligible to vote until the autumn", an effective 3918, and the percentage poll "was 48.85". Hourly figures end "8, 1913, including 16 postal votes". (1913/3918 is 48.83%; the DB stores 48.8.) Halcrow is "the first woman candidate to be successful at the Lerwick poll for nineteen years". statutory meeting "last Friday night" (7 May). New junior Bailie Robert B. Blance "was third (only 21 votes behind the top-of-the poll candidate) in last week's municipal election". Miss Grace M. T. Halcrow welcomed as the new member, and the three retiring members who were successful.
"RETIRING COUNCILLORS": "Retiring Councillors in May are Bailie W. K. Conochie, Dean of Guild Arthur Johnson, and Councillors J. G. Peterson and J. W. Tait".
"Tuesday first is the Town Council polling day"
"County election on Tuesday". Electors in seven parishes go to the poll "on Tuesday first, 10th". The baseline's Thursday 5 May has no support.

retiring are Provost Burgess, ex-Provost Anderson, Councillors Eunson, Gray and Johnson: "the first four retire by rotation, the last-mentioned as a co-opted member". All five were returned unopposed.
"No municipal election this year": the first since the war. Nominations closed on the Tuesday.

"NO ELECTION THIS YEAR": "only the four retiring councillors had been nominated": Robert B. Blance, Alexander Morrison, Andrew J. Nicolson, Robert Ollason. Grace Halcrow is not among them (the wiki has her).
statutory meeting; the Provost thanked "the four retiring members" for standing again.
John W. Eunson's resignation "was accepted by the Council at Tuesday night's meeting" (14 Jan 1958).
on the Provost's casting vote, a special meeting decided to leave Eunson's seat vacant until the May election.

Bailie Tait and Councillor Daniel "have been longest on the Council, and automatically retire". The other two places were drawn by lot from the five who entered unopposed in 1956 (Anderson, Burgess, Eunson, H. Gray, Johnson), Eunson included: "Out came G. H. Burgess and A. Johnson". So five vacancies in May.
"Six County Council elections". The sitting member for Cunningsburgh, Miss Grace Halcrow, "is being opposed by Mrs Joan McLeod", the first time a division had an all-female choice.
"County elections". "Tuesday first is polling day in the county." Halcrow "has withdrawn from Cunningsburgh", leaving McLeod returned unopposed.
"With poor weather on Tuesday" (result report)
"Three out of five were very close". Polling took place in five County Council elections "on Tuesday": 13 May.
Tait, the poll-topper made Bailie and Dean of Guild, "has had to intimate his resignation" (date not given).

"Bailie J. W. Tait's departure". His formal resignation was submitted "at last Tuesday's Council meeting" (Tue 17 Jun 1958), leaving the Council to fix the operative date. The Council "decided not to appoint a successor until next Tuesday", so he "left Shetland as a Bailie" (on Sat 14 Jun). The town clerk said a resignation normally took effect after three weeks, or earlier if the notice gave a da
special meeting "on Tuesday night" (24 Jun 1958): the vacancy from "the recent retiral of Bailie J. W. Tait" filled by co-opting Arthur Johnson.

retiring by rotation: Provost Conochie ("four years without facing a contest"), Bailie Harry Gray and ex-Provost Anderson ("three years"), Councillor A. J. Nicolson ("two years (his place was decided by lot some months ago)"), and Arthur Johnson, co-opted after the last election.
"the Town Council election on the 5th May, 1959" (OCR "sth")
at the monthly meeting "on Tuesday" (11 Aug 1959) a letter from M. J. Sandison resigning (he might be employed by the Education Department).
ex-Bailie Harry Gray, top of the unsuccessful in May, "was co-opted to the Town Council last Thursday" (3 Sep 1959).
"Eight candidates for five seats". Ollason decided not to re-stand; "the other four retiring councillors" (marked *) are Daniel, Eric Gray, Harry Gray and Morrison. Blance (Provost) is not retiring.
due to retire in May: Burgess, Strachan, Conochie, Johnson.
News in brief. Five County Council elections "a week from Tuesday", i.e. Tuesday 9 May.
"Shocks for retiring councillors". The count for all five was in the County Buildings "on Wednesday afternoon" (10 May), the day after polling.
"Newly-elected councillor resigns": the Rev. Kenneth Thomson, third in the poll, resigned at Friday's statutory meeting (5 May 1961); he held a teaching post and was ineligible.

"Co-opted to Town Council": Robert Strachan, who headed the unsuccessful candidates, co-opted at "Tuesday's Town Council meeting" (13 Jun 1961) for Thomson's vacancy. The wiki's "By-Election May 1961" was this June co-option.

"RETIRING COUNCILLORS": Provost R. B. Blance, elected May 1957 and on the council without an election since, "owing to his elevation to the Provost's chair in 1959"; Anderson and Nicolson, elected 1959; James J. Paton, "lowest of the successful candidates in 1960"; and Robert Strachan, co-opted last June.
the Town Council report of the July meeting (Tue 3 Jul) covers the Planning Committee (the Post Office engineering centre site). The OCR has no mention of Daniel, a resignation or a vacancy.
M. M. Shearer co-opted to replace J. A. Daniel, "who recently submitted his resignation" (date not given).
four vacancies. Ex-Provost Conochie is not seeking re-election; the other retiring members are Eric Gray, Morrison and Shearer. Harry Gray is not retiring.
Halcrow "was elected to the Town Council ten years ago, but served for only one year before resigning" for the county council. Confirms she was not on the council 1957–60.
"on Election Day, Tuesday, 5th of May" (OCR "sth")
News in brief. The County and District Council elections "take place in Shetland on Tuesday first", with counts on the Wednesday.
"THE RESULT". Successful: J. J. Taylor 820, Miss Halcrow 799, A. Johnson 753, P. Robertson 741; A. I. Anderson (686) lost. Same figures as the baseline.
"NO MUNICIPAL ELECTION": only the four retiring members were nominated (Anderson, H. Gray, Nicolson, Paton: the four returned).

"Only one new council aspirant". There were five candidates for four seats: the retiring Senior Bailie Eric Gray, Junior Bailie Robert Adair, Dean of Guild Alex. Morrison and Magnus Shearer, plus John R. Smith (Labour, county councillor for Bressay). A poll was set for 3 May.
"No election". Junior Bailie Adair (Labour) "decided not to seek re-election", so the four remaining candidates were returned unopposed.
Same page (art. 059, "News in brief"): ten candidates for four seats; "All four retiring members": Miss Grace Halcrow, Arthur Johnson, Peter Robertson and James J. Taylor.

ST Fri 14 Apr 1967, p4 (art. 061, "First election in three years"): at Tuesday's meeting (11 Apr) the council heard Provost A. J. Nicolson "is having to resign because of ill-health"; the resignation "becomes effective on 27th April", and the council would probably co-opt an unsuccessful candidate. He had joined in 1955, Bailie 1959, Provost 1965.

ST Fri 12 May 1967, p3 (art. 046, "He will be Provost for one year"): "Miss Grace Halcrow was co-opted, in place of Provost A. J. Nicolson ... at the statutory meeting of the council last Friday night" (5 May). Eric Gray was made Provost at the Tuesday meeting (9 May), since the Provostship vacancy needed five days' notice.
obituary. "On Sunday morning" Shetland lost ex-Provost Robert A. Anderson, at home at 9 North Lochside, aged 64.
death notice, "on 25th June, 1967, Robert Andrew".
Ronald P. Cumming "has been co-opted as a Lerwick town councillor in succession to the late ex-Provost R. A. Anderson"; he was an unsuccessful May candidate. Harry Gray became Hon. Treasurer.

Same issue, p5 (art. 094, "Faroe gift"): "At Tuesday night's Town Council meeting" (8 Aug). The co-option isn't dated in the paper, but the only meeting that week was Tuesday's, and the 4 Aug paper doesn't mention it (cumming council, 23 Jun–25 Aug: one hit, 11 Aug).

ST Fri 15 Mar 1968, p5 (art. 078, "Four retiring councillors"): due to retire in May are "the Hon. Treasurer Harry Gray, Mr J. J. Paton, and the two co-opted members, Miss" (Halcrow) and Cumming (from the snippet; the four are the 1965 cohort's seats).

"Eight candidates for four seats". Nominations closed on Tuesday. Paton (Lab.), Halcrow, Cumming and H. Gray (Ind.) seek re-election; the new candidates include W. P. L. Thomson and Robert Adair (Lab.) and Tom Moncrieff (Ind.), now eligible because the town's seats on the County Council were cut from twelve to nine. "Polling takes place in Lerwick on 7th May."

"The result". Successful: Cumming 791, H. Gray 724, W. Thomson 686, Halcrow 577. Unsuccessful: Paton 573, Adair 555, Moncrieff 399, D. Leask 372. These are the same figures as the baseline. The council stays eight Independent and four Labour.

retiring are "Messrs M. M. Shearer, A. Morrison, J. R. Smith (all elected in 1966) and W A. Smith (least successful candidate in 1967)". Eric Gray, also elected in 1966, is Provost and not in the list.
"THE RESULT". Successful: Alex. Morrison 1290, James J. Paton 1060, W. A. Smith 1054, John R. Smith 893; Furnival 807 and Moncrieff 557 lost. Same as the baseline.
"Both Lerwick's bailies are due to retire by rotation": Bailies Robertson and Taylor, G. W. Blance and Miss G. M. T. Halcrow.
seven candidates for four seats; Blance and Taylor re-stand, Robertson and Halcrow "did not lodge papers" (she blamed the winter's weather).
"on Tuesday night a letter from Mr John R. Smith was read, intimating his resignation" (Tue 14 Apr 1970). The council "will be one member short when the result is declared".
Adair co-opted "at Friday's statutory meeting" (Fri 8 May 1970) as "the unsuccessful candidate with the highest number of votes".
"Five members ... are due to retire in May": Provost Eric Gray, Hon. Treas. Harry Gray, R. P. Cumming, W. P. Thomson and R. Adair.

retiring before the 2 May election are "Mr Alex. Morrison, Mr J. J. Paton, Mr W. Peterson and Mr A. J. R. Tait". Peterson and Tait were elected in 1970; W. A. Smith (1969) is Provost and not in the list.
no election "for the second year in succession"; four nominations (Laurenson, and retiring Morrison, Paton, Peterson). Provost W. A. Smith regretted Tait was not standing.

"For the third year in succession" no poll: "only the four retiring councillors had been nominated". The list is Blance, Butler, and (OCR cut off) the other two; the 1973 winners are Blance, Butler, E. Gray and Taylor.

"Town Council Election. Nine Candidates for Five Seats": poll Tue 1 Nov 1932; four retiring members stand (Bruce, Manson, Morrison, Sandison); ex-Provost R. D. Ganson, elected 1911, does not seek re-election.
"The Municipal Election. Eight Candidates for Four Seats": the four retiring Councillors are Provost W. Sinclair, Bailie Ollason, ex-Provosts J. Laing and J. T. J. Sinclair; poll Tue 7 Nov 1933.

"Four Candidates for Five Seats": no poll; Halcrow, Irvine, Shearer and T. A. Sinclair to be declared elected Tue 3 Nov 1936. Irvine and T. A. Sinclair were co-opted; Provost Ollason and C. A. Manson, retiring, did not seek re-election.
Acting Chief Magistrate C. G. Duncan certifies Arthur James Hay and John Robertson senior elected Senior and Junior Bailie on 3 Sep 1874: the first group (paper then dated Mondays).
Notice: the first election of Town Council under the Lerwick Act of 1876 on Tuesday 7 Nov 1876; twelve to be elected.
Result of the poll, 7 Nov 1876: twelve elected in order (Hunter 119 to L. G. Stove 69), six not; 252 on the roll and 187 voted.
Notice: annual election of four councillors on Tuesday 6 Nov 1877; nominations by Thursday 1 Nov.
The four retiring Councillors (Jamieson, W. Robertson, Leisk, Stove) re-nominated, no other nominations, no poll.
Special meeting on Thursday (24 Jan 1878) to fill the vacancy caused by the resignation of Bailie Sievwright: John Robertson junior unanimously elected.
Town Clerk's notice of 1 Nov 1878: Arthur J. Hay, John Robertson sen., John Robertson jun. and Robert Sinclair proposed; no more than the vacancies, so no poll.
Four retiring: Major Cameron, G. H. B. Hay and James Hunter re-nominated; Arthur Laurenson would not allow himself to be re-nominated, leaving a vacancy.
W. Robertson, Jamieson, L. G. Stove and Leisk re-nominated and James M. Goudie nominated for the other vacancy; no poll.
William Duncan, elected at the last meeting to the place vacant by the resignation of James M. Goudie, took the oath.
Notice: election of councillors to supply five vacancies on Tuesday 1 Nov 1881; nominations by Thursday 27 Oct.

Five vacancies: Bailies Robertson and Hay, Robert Sinclair and J. Robertson jr retire in rotation and Duncan (elected to a vacancy) must seek re-election; Sinclair not standing, James Tulloch jr nominated; no poll.
Of the four retiring, Major Cameron, James Hunter and James Tulloch re-nominated; Mr Hay not; Alexander Mitchell nominated for the fourth vacancy.
Five vacancies: Jamieson, Leisk and L. G. Stove whose term has expired, the resignation of Major Cameron and the decease of William Robertson.
Jamieson, Leisk and L. G. Stove re-nominated; Frank H. Halcrow and Gilbert Harrison nominated to the other two vacancies.
New councillors: Leisk, Stove, Jamieson, Halcrow and Harrison attended and declared their acceptance.

"Election of a Councillor": the first business was filling the vacancy caused by the resignation of Bailie Hay; Leisk proposed William Duncan, merchant. The meeting day is not in the sub-articles; it came after the annual meeting of Monday 10 Nov.
Adjourned meeting on Tuesday evening (18 Nov 1884): W. Duncan among those present.

Nominations on Thursday: retiring by rotation John Robertson (Chief Magistrate), Charles Robertson (Junior Bailie), John Robertson jr, J. B. Anderson and A. A. Porteous, all re-nominated, to be declared elected on Tuesday next.
Nominations on Thursday for the four vacancies: the retiring councillors were re-nominated and will be declared elected on the appointed day.
Retiring: Provost Robertson, Bailie Laurenson, John Robertson and A. A. Porteous; Laurenson has intimated he will not stand.
Laurenson refused to seek re-election and P. S. Goodlad was nominated; "on Tuesday next, the day of election", the four to be declared elected.
Monthly meeting on Tuesday evening (4 Apr 1899) sat in committee to appoint a Councillor in place of the late A. J. Garriock: Sinclair Johnson elected.
Monthly meeting on Tuesday evening (2 May 1899): Sinclair Johnson, "elected at last meeting" for Garriock, took the affirmation and his seat.
"Appointment of a Town Councillor": special meeting on Tuesday at noon (28 Feb 1905).
"New member co-opted" at the monthly meeting on Tuesday evening (6 May 1924): E. S. Reid Tait co-opted to the casual vacancy caused by the resignation of James Goodlad.
Result of the Tuesday poll (3 Nov 1925): Campbell 763 ... Morrison 518 (other figures garbled in the OCR); 1305 polled of a roll of 2099.
Result of the Tuesday poll (2 Nov 1926): Ganson, Ratter, Sandison, Irvine elected; J. Manson, Murray, Gray, Spence not. Total poll 1196. The figures are in a table the OCR lost.
Result: W. Sinclair 780, L. Sandison 756, A. S. Manson 514, R. D. Ganson (figure garbled), then Irvine and Ratter, "retiring members", defeated.
Monthly meeting (day lost in the OCR): a letter from Bailie Campbell tendering his resignation from the Town Council.
Cogle appointed Junior Bailie; James Morrison, a former member, co-opted a Councillor in place of Bailie Campbell.
"Council vacancy": T. A. Sinclair, the only nominee for the vacancy caused through the death of David Gray, duly elected at the meeting on Tuesday (2 Apr 1946; art. 073).
"Decisions from the Council": R. B. Blance, top of the unsuccessful candidates at the last election, co-opted to the vacancy caused by the resignation of J. A. Jamieson.
Full list of the 27 divisions with electors (men and women), polls and votes; Fetlar, Walls North and Walls South had no nomination.
"The polling for Eastern Division of this parish took place" at Ollaberry on Tuesday (4 Feb).
Contests preview: Lerwick unopposed; in North Delting "Mr Hoseason intimates that he is ineligible, and Pole will be duly returned".

"The Nominations": at the close on Tuesday (22 Nov) nineteen seats were unopposed, five had two candidates and three (Burra, Walls, Fetlar) had none. Aithsting: Grierson and McCullie nominated; Grierson also returned unopposed for Sandness.

"The polling for the contested divisions took place on Tuesday" (6 Dec). Unst North Sandison 71 Edmondston 28; Delting North Inkster 17 to 2; Sandwick Duncan v Tulloch 21; Tingwall Hay 80 Downes 79. McCullie "had practically a walk over" in Aithsting.

Nominations for every division: all single except Tingwall (A. J. Hay and W. P. Harcus). Sinclair Johnson's nomination for Aithsting fell through (not on the roll), so a new election will be ordered there.
Tingwall: the election "took place on Tuesday" (3 Dec); counted the next day: Hay 95, Harcus 84.

Nominations: contests in Sandsting (Garriock the sitting member v Inkster Harcus and Mitchell), Nesting (Small v Hunter), Burra (Henderson the sitting member v Lennie) and Dunrossness North (Rev. Charles Whyte v Isbister); no nomination in Delting South.

"The voting for County Councillors for Sandsting, Burra Isle, and Nesting took place on Tuesday" (6 Dec). Mitchell top in Sandsting, Lennie in Burra, Small in Nesting (figures lost in the OCR); list of the new Council.
New elections ordered for Sandsting and Aithsting: nominations on the 28th, "and polling if necessary on the 11th April"; the transposed voters' lists to be put right.
Sandsting: Archibald J. Garriock returned unopposed; Aithsting: James Anderson, the sitting member, opposed by Gilbert Williamson.
"On Saturday last" (29 Mar) the Deputy Returning Officer declared Rev. J. A. Campbell elected for Fetlar and Peter Georgeson for Walls (Southern division).

Garriock told of his election for Sandsting on Monday (14 Apr); the Aithsting result made known on Tuesday (figures lost). Walls North and Delting still unrepresented; the Delting councillor had resigned and the County Council would fill it after 15 May.

First meeting of the County Council: James Inkster, Brae, unanimously appointed for North Delting, vacant by the resignation of C. Hoseason. Walls North deferred (rival names; referred to the Secretary for Scotland).
Annual meeting of the County Council ("Tuesday noon", art. 038): James M. Goudie unanimously appointed to fill the vacancy caused by the death of Arthur Laurenson.
Notice of the annual meeting on Thursday 19th instant at noon: "To fill up the vacancy in the Council caused by the resignation of Mr James H. Sutherland".
"At the meeting of the County Council held on Thursday" (19 May) Dr Yule was elected Medical Officer.
The Secretary for Scotland has fixed Tuesday 24 January for the election of a County Councillor for each of Fetlar, Burra and Quarff, and Walls; nominations by 10 January.
Two nominations, so a contest in Fetlar; Georgeson and Gray (who had represented Walls and Burra) are returned unopposed.
Fetlar: "On Tuesday last week the election ... took place" (24 Jan); Nicolson v Rev. W. Glover; the ballot reached the Returning Officer on Mon 30 Jan and was counted on Tuesday (figures lost).
Aithsting "came off Tuesday" (14 Jan): Johnston 56, Tulloch 0, two spoiled; Tulloch "took not the slightest interest".
Letter from Rev. George Clark, Cunningsburgh, resigning owing to the state of his health.
Adjourned meeting "on Thursday at noon" (4 Jun): on a petition from Cunningsburgh ratepayers J. M. Tulloch was appointed in room of Rev. George Clark.
Monthly meeting "on Thursday at noon" (4 Feb): on a petition A. Cunningham Hay was unanimously appointed for Tingwall in room of his late uncle.
Monthly meeting "on Wednesday at noon" (3 Nov): on a petition of 118 ratepayers Andrew Robertson was appointed for Northmavine North in room of George Sinclair, resigned.
Monthly meeting (Thursday, 3 Feb): rival petitions for Burra, Lennie's with 113 signatures; the Council preferred the local man and Henderson was "duly elected". No poll.
"The Dunrossness vacancy": at the meeting of Thursday (4 Aug) no one from the parish had been put forward for Henderson's seat; left over "till the September meeting".
Monthly meeting: the only person willing was Rev. Charles Whyte, and his appointment for Dunrossness North was agreed unanimously.
The Secretary for Scotland has ordered a new election for Delting (South) on 24 January.
Mr William J. Adie, merchant, Voe, has been nominated for the vacancy in South Delting.

Nominations closed Tuesday (19 Nov): single nominations everywhere but Tingwall (Duncan, Leslie, Holborn), Nesting, Lerwick North and both Northmavines; no nomination in Unst South, Fetlar and Yell South.
Polling "on Tuesday first"; "The only withdrawal" is Holborn of Foula, so Tingwall is Duncan v Leslie.
"The election in the contested divisions of Northmavine, Nesting, Tingwall, and Lerwick took place on Tuesday" (3 Dec).

The result: Tulloch over Robertson (Lerwick North), Duncan over Leslie (Tingwall), Robertson over Hughson (majority 35), Anderson over Wallace, Small over Johnson (two spoiled papers would have made it equal); most figures lost in the OCR.
"NEW ELECTIONS": an Order by the Secretary for Scotland fixing a day this month (lost in the OCR) for the election of County Councillors for Unst South, Fetlar and Yell South.
Nominations for the three divisions: Unst South J. P. Sandison, Fetlar Sir Arthur Nicolson, Yell South David Williamson; "there will be no poll".
Monthly meeting "Thursday at noon" (6 Feb): the Clerk reported Sandison, Nicolson and Williamson elected for the three divisions; Williamson already present.
Papa Stour: J. G. Holborn of Foula, "the new representative in the County Council" of the northern ward of Walls (Sandness), visited on Saturday last.
"RESIGNATION OF A COUNCILLOR": W. J. Adie's letter resigning as Councillor for Delting South.
Meeting "Thursday at noon" (16 Apr): James A. Adie unanimously appointed for South Delting in place of W. J. Adie, resigned owing to ill health.
Adjourned general meeting "on Thursday at noon" (17 Sep): on an Ollaberry petition of 4 Sep, R. Camperdown Haldane appointed for Northmavine North, unanimously.

"County Council Nominations": complete list; two each in Northmavine North, Delting North (Inkster and Pole), Whiteness and Weisdale, Lerwick Central (Jamieson and Henderson) and Sandwick; Walls no nomination.

"Polling ... took place Tuesday last" (6 Dec) in four contested divisions: Haldane v Loggie, Pole v J. Inkster, P. Anderson v H. J. Robertson, W. Smith v J. Thomson (figures lost); list of the new Council.
Walls County Council election: a new election ordered by the Secretary for Scotland; nominations 31st inst., "the election for 14th February".
"NEW ELECTION": the Clerk reported that Mr Holborn, of Foula, had been elected County Councillor for Walls.
Monthly meeting: the appointment for Yell North in place of the late Mr Hamilton deferred, so the district could name a candidate.
"ZETLAND COUNTY COUNCIL": the monthly meeting "on Thursday at noon" (15 Feb 1906).
"COUNCILLOR FOR NORTH YELL": on the ratepayers' recommendation T. J. Sandison, Uyeasound, unanimously elected in place of the late Mr Hamilton.
County Council: on a requisition from electors of the north of the parish, James Budge, farmer, unanimously elected for Dunrossness in place of the late R. H. Isbister; meeting day lost in the OCR.
"ZETLAND COUNTY COUNCIL": the monthly meeting "on Thursday of last week" (15 Aug 1907).
"THE DUNROSSNESS VACANCY": on a petition, Rev. W. Fotheringham unanimously elected in room of the late John Bruce of Sumburgh.

"NOMINATION OF CANDIDATES" (Tuesday 19 Nov): complete list; contests possible in Yell South, Delting North, Delting South, Walls (three), Sandsting, Aithsting, Northmavine North and Whalsay; Sandwick Mr W. Smith alone; voting Tuesday 3rd December.

Withdrawals: Shearer (Whalsay) and Laurence (Yell South) withdrew, Leslie's Aithsting nomination informal; five contests remain (Delting North, Delting South, Walls, Sandsting, Northmavine North); "The poll takes place on Tuesday first, 3rd December".
Leader on the results: in Walls, of "the 104 votes cast, he received 69" (Thomason); J. P. Henderson's return for Delting "looked for".
"RESULTS OF THE POLLS": voting in the five contested divisions "on Tuesday last" (3 Dec); counted Thursday.
Results (figures lost): Sandsting J. B. Anderson over W. Robertson; Walls Thomason, Harcus, Holborn; Northmavine North Thomas Anderson over Haldane.
Results (figures lost): Delting South L. Robertson over J. A. Adie; Delting North J. P. Henderson over A. White.
"COUNCILLOR FOR TINGWALL": on a ratepayers' petition L. J. Garriock unanimously elected for W. Rae Duncan, resigned, at the monthly meeting "on Thursday forenoon" (18 Mar).
County Council: a petition for R. Inkster, Scalloway, in place of the late Mr Lennie; the Clerk to give notice of the vacancy for the next meeting.
Monthly meeting "on Thursday" (12 Aug): two petitions for Robert Inkster to fill the vacancy caused by the death of C. Lennie; moved and elected.
"NEW COUNTY COUNCILLOR": on a Parish Council petition James Shearer, Symbister, unanimously elected for Whalsay in room of Rev. C. Stobie, resigned; the meeting was "on Thursday last week" (21 Jul).
